editorial.headline: Sheet Glass Wholesale: Nationally Open, Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers wholesale sheet glass for construction, but Bali’s island-wide PMA moratorium prevents foreign investment registration there today.
editorial.body:
Sheet-glass wholesale is a construction-material trade activity: the wholesale supply of clear sheet glass, frosted sheet glass, coloured clear sheet glass and engraved sheet glass. Its subject is specific and material-led. The activity concerns sheet glass sold wholesale for use as a building material, rather than a broader description of construction work or a generic retail proposition.

It is open across the full stated business-scale range: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. At the national level, its PMA status is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In straightforward terms, the national record allows foreign ownership up to that ceiling for this activity. The cited PMA basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

Bali changes the practical answer for a foreign investor. The Bali status is blocked at the risk-class level, and PMA registration is blocked. The record explains that, at the Besar scale, every scope is assessed in OSS as Rendah or Menengah-Rendah; this places the activity within Bali’s moratorium. That moratorium, dated May 2026 in the record, blocks PMA for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI across the province on a permanent, island-wide basis.

The distinction matters because national openness is not the same as present availability for PMA registration in Bali. A founder can accurately say that the activity is nationally open to foreign ownership up to 100%; they cannot accurately conclude from that fact alone that a foreign-owned registration is available in Bali today. For Bali, the current answer is clear: a foreigner cannot register this activity for PMA under the stated moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness is not the same as present availability for PMA registration in Bali.
